subject: Hospitality
title: Caravanserais of the Silk Road
description: Learn Caravanserais of the Silk Road in one minute.

hook.text: Across the Silk Road, fortified inns called caravanserais sheltered merchants, camels, and goods every 30 km.

buildup.text: These stone complexes had courtyards for animals, rooms for traders, and kitchens. Many were free, funded by rulers.

discovery.text: Caravanserais weren't just lodging—they were trading hubs where cultures, languages, and goods mixed freely.

twist.text: Sultans built them strategically. A safe trade route meant more commerce, more taxes, and more political power.

climax.text: Thousands were built from Turkey to China. Some still stand today, converted into boutique hotels.

punchline.text: Free lodging, strategic power. Ancient hotels were foreign policy.

quiz.question: Why did rulers fund caravanserais along the Silk Road?
options: Safe trade routes meant more commerce and taxes
